verses.text: Does being one with Christ encourage you? Does his love comfort you? Do you share in the Spirit? Do you have tender kindness and care?
Then make my joy complete by agreeing with each other. Have the same love. Be united in spirit and in purpose.
Do nothing out of selfish ambition or pride. Instead, be humble, and think of others as better than yourselves.
Each of you should look not only to your own interests, but also to the interests of others.
Have the same attitude that Christ Jesus had.
He was God by nature, yet he did not think being equal with God was something to hold on to.
Instead, he gave up everything and took the nature of a servant. He was born as a human being.
And when he appeared as a man, he humbled himself. He obeyed God even to the point of death, yes, death on a cross!
So God raised him to the highest place. He gave him the name that is above every name.
So at the name of Jesus every knee will bow, in heaven and on earth and under the earth.
And every tongue will say that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
So, my dear friends, you have always obeyed, not only when I was with you. Now that I am away, obey even more. Keep working out your salvation with respect and trembling.
It is God who works in you, to make you want and do what pleases him.
Do everything without grumbling or arguing.
Then you will be pure and without blame, children of God without fault, in a crooked and twisted world. You will shine among them like stars in the sky,
as you hold firmly to the word of life. Then I can be proud on the day of Christ that I did not run my race or work hard for nothing.
Your faith is like an offering to God. Even if my life is poured out like a drink offering on it, I am glad. I share my joy with all of you.
In the same way, you too should be glad and share your joy with me.
I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon. Then I too will be cheered when I hear news about you.
I have no one else like him, who truly cares about how you are.
All the others look after their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ.
But you know that Timothy has proved himself. He has worked with me for the Good News, like a son with his father.
So I hope to send him as soon as I see how things go with me.
And I trust in the Lord that I myself will come soon too.
But I think I must send Epaphroditus back to you. He is my brother, my co-worker and fellow soldier. You sent him to help me in my need.
He longs for all of you, and he is upset because you heard he was ill.
He was indeed ill, and he nearly died. But God had mercy on him, and on me too, so that I would not have sorrow on top of sorrow.
So I am all the more eager to send him. Then when you see him again you will be glad, and I will worry less.
Welcome him in the Lord with great joy, and honour people like him.
He almost died for the work of Christ. He risked his life to give me the help that you could not give.
